issue.description:
Parent: the R041 umbrella (unique ref agent-friction:umbrella). Spec-first child: every implementation child is blocked on this one. Evidence is on the umbrella.

Deliverables:
- docs/plan/plan.md: add `R041 - Agent-ergonomic CLI surface` with the umbrella's evidence summary and a revision note.
- research/specs/agent-ergonomics-v1.md (new), plus revisions to research/specs/native-field-guide-v1.md section 3.1 (today: list emits one object per line, show emits a one-element array; it also still says show omits `notes`, which is stale) and research/specs/needle-cli-contract-v1.md (show and list rows; claim-credential environment).

The product decisions below are settled. The spec writes them down and defines their edge cases, error text, exit codes and conformance scenario names; it does not reopen them:
1. JSON documents. `list --json` prints exactly one JSON array, `[]` when empty; new `--jsonl` keeps the one-object-per-line stream. `show ID --json` prints one JSON object. `create --json` prints the created issue as one object; plain `create` keeps printing only the ID (NEEDLE contract). `capabilities` advertises the shapes so consumers can feature-detect.
2. Claim credential from the environment. When a claimant-owned mutation targets the issue named by NEEDLE_BEAD_ID and no `--fencing-token` is given, the credential is read from NEEDLE_BEAD_FENCING_TOKEN. An explicit flag wins; a mutation on any other issue ignores both variables; the audit event records the credential source. Every mutating command accepts `--fencing-token`, including label add/remove and dep add/remove: those stay unfenced on omission, but a supplied token is validated exactly as on fenced surfaces.
3. Text input. `update --append-notes TEXT` appends inside the mutation transaction (the spec fixes the separator); `--notes-file PATH|-`, `close --reason-file PATH|-`, `create --description-file PATH|-`. Values beginning with `-` are accepted for --notes, --append-notes, --reason, --description and --title. Exactly one notes source per call. State how --append-notes relates to native comments (R010, beadrs-2ddcb210) so agents know which to use for what.
4. Read shortcuts. `bead ready` = `list --ready`; `bead search TEXT` = `list --all --search TEXT`; `list --all` (every status); `list --search TEXT` (case-insensitive substring over title, description and notes; combines with other filters); `list --count`; `dep list ID` (blockers and dependents with kind and blocker status); `bead ID` behaves as `show ID` only when the token has the workspace's issue-ID shape, and a subcommand name always wins.
5. `bead history ID [--json]`: one issue's events in order, redaction-aware, distinct from the workspace-wide `bead changes` feed.
6. `label add|remove ID LABEL...`: positional labels alongside the existing `--label`.

Also record in the plan's Open questions (not implemented by R041): whether title/description/priority should become editable through an audited operation, citing the umbrella's evidence against R037/ADR-007.

Clean-room note: the new command spellings come from our own agents' observed invocations in our own transcripts (public process-boundary facts). Author all prose independently.

Acceptance:
- Plan R041 and the spec files are committed and pushed; every decision above has defined error and exit behaviour plus named conformance scenarios the implementation children can cite.
- The NEEDLE impact is stated: NEEDLE's show parsers already accept an object (every show parse site in NEEDLE src/bead_store/cli_store.rs falls back from array to object), and the contract's list row already permits an array, so no NEEDLE code change is expected.
issue.notes: R041 specification was already published at 16ff821a and remains present in the four owned paths: docs/plan/plan.md, research/specs/agent-ergonomics-v1.md, research/specs/native-field-guide-v1.md, and research/specs/needle-cli-contract-v1.md. The plan records the umbrella evidence summary, spec-first revision note, NEEDLE impact, and the R037/ADR-007 Open question; the normative spec defines all six settled decisions, exact diagnostics and exit classes, and 24 AE scenarios. To make the committed R041 implementation gate pass, this attempt also repaired two stale list --json consumers in tests/r013_change_feed.rs and tests/redact_all_blocking.rs (commits 86b2d288 and c81164e6); both targeted suites pass. Final delivery: pushed origin/main through c81164e6; git rev-list origin/main..HEAD is empty. Clean git archive HEAD verification passed scripts/definition-of-done.sh --fast (fmt + cargo test, including R041 and NEEDLE suites); final cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check passed. The earlier shared-tree and pre-repair archive failures are superseded by this final committed-state pass.

Stale-event merge replay conformance for unknown fields is landed and pushed (revision 3f159eb on origin main). The generation conformance suite now exercises all three replay outcomes for the extension-bearing event. Idempotent replay - merging the log the destination restored from - must leave the stored extension map exactly as stored, asserted immediately before the later replays rewrite the same map. Widen - a newer producer replays the seeded future_tier value grown with nested shapes plus an additive future_tier_replayed key - must replace the stored map outright. issue.description:
Split child of beadrs-8923aef3; depends on beadrs-436f74b7 (redaction path). Stale-event merge replay is the second path that rewrites historical records. Add/verify a conformance test covering all three replay outcomes for events carrying unknown extensions: idempotent replay (same producer value replays with extensions intact), widen (a newer producer's wider unknown value replaces the older one — widen-never-erase), and strip/narrow (an older or narrower replay must never erase what an earlier generation stored). The migration-related implementation is expected to express this as widen-never-erase replay semantics; the test is what locks it.
Acceptance criteria:
- All three replay outcomes (idempotent, widen, strip/narrow) are exercised against unknown-field-bearing events.
- Widening replaces the extension value; narrowing/idempotent replay provably preserves the stored extension (assert a would-be erasure fails the test).
- Suite green locally; evidence recorded on this bead.
issue.notes: Landed the prior attempt's unstaged test work as revision 3f159eb, pushed to origin main. The stale-event merge replay section of tests/checkpoint_unknown_field_generation_conformance.rs now exercises all three replay outcomes on the extension-bearing event: idempotent replay leaves the stored extension map exactly as stored (asserted before later replays rewrite it), widen replaces the stored map outright with the newer producer's wider value (seeded future_tier grown with nested shapes plus an additive future_tier_replayed key), and strip/narrow requires exact equality with the widened map so any value change fails, not just key removal. Negative half proves a would-be erasure fails the suite: dropping the seeded key, dropping the widened key, and narrowing the widened value back to the older producer's each trip the preservation assertion by name. Verified on a clean git-archive extraction of pushed HEAD (target cache copied in): full definition-of-done passed, 1564 tests green including all 3 conformance tests. A fleet checkpoint publish (6df14bf) landed on top afterward - .beads checkpoint files only, no source delta.

issue.description:
src/store/sqlite.rs:58-75 and src/store/mod.rs:116-131 deliberately configure every store connection with PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=5000, journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL. But ~25 command handlers in src/main.rs open raw rusqlite::Connection::open(&db_path) with NONE of these (lines 109, 271, 308, 379, 443, 488, 517, 552, 600, 622, 651, 726, 777, 808, 833, 873, 918, 1034, 1468, 1619, 2110, 2263, 2356), as do src/service/doctor.rs:451 and 495.

Consequences: (a) SQLite foreign_keys defaults OFF per-connection, so every 'FOREIGN KEY ... ON DELETE CASCADE' declared in src/store/migrations.rs (lines 128-412) is unenforced on the CLI's primary code paths; (b) busy_timeout=0 means concurrent fleet access (multiple workers running bead claim/update against one workspace, the tool's core use case) hits immediate SQLITE_BUSY -> exit 1 instead of waiting up to 5s, undermining the concurrent-claim contract documented in README 'Coordinating a fleet'. cmd_claim (main.rs:102-116) also uses unchecked_transaction (deferred) on such a raw connection.

Fix: add one shared helper (e.g. in src/store) that opens + applies the same pragmas as SqliteStore, and use it from every handler in main.rs and doctor.rs; remove direct Connection::open calls there.

Acceptance (run in repo):
1. grep -n "Connection::open(" src/main.rs src/service/doctor.rs returns no raw call sites (only the shared helper, or nothing).
2. A test asserts the connection used by a representative handler has foreign_keys=1 and busy_timeout=5000 (query 'PRAGMA foreign_keys; PRAGMA busy_timeout;').
3. cargo test passes.
issue.notes:
Shipped in 4d08718 (pushed to origin/main).

What changed:
- src/store exposes open_configured_connection() -- single pragma configuration point (foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=5000, journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL). SqliteStore internals and workspace discovery now route through it too (discovery previously set only 2 of the 4 pragmas).
- All 27 raw Connection::open sites in main.rs (25 handler sites + the publication-chokepoint helper + the post-restore publication path) and all 7 in doctor.rs now use it. Acceptance grep 'grep -n "Connection::open(" src/main.rs src/service/doctor.rs' returns nothing; the only Connection::open left in src/ is inside the helper itself (plus recurrence.rs test code, out of scope).
- tests/connection_pragmas.rs: asserts foreign_keys=1 / busy_timeout=5000 / journal_mode=wal / synchronous=1 via the PRAGMA queries on the shared opener every handler uses, plus a functional test proving the timeout waits out a held WAL write lock instead of failing immediately.

Acceptance (cargo test): full suite run on HEAD+this-change: 43/44 test binaries green; the one failure (test_sync_flush_only_rejects_invalid_profile, cli_sync) fails identically on pure HEAD -- pre-existing residue of the b9cdef9 --profile removal, whose fix is already in another worker's uncommitted tests/cli_sync.rs. Both new tests pass in the live tree as well.

Finding worth a follow-up (filed as a new bead): SQLite does NOT invoke the busy handler when a DEFERRED transaction that has already read tries to upgrade to a write transaction -- that returns immediate SQLITE_BUSY regardless of busy_timeout. All mutating handlers use unchecked_transaction() (deferred), so handler-vs-handler write contention still fails fast; the pragma fix covers lock-acquisition paths (autocommit writes, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, publication) and foreign_keys enforcement. Converting mutating handlers to BEGIN IMMEDIATE is the separate fix.

Concurrency note: verified and committed while R035/R036 workers had uncommitted edits in the same files; the commit was staged from the exact verified HEAD+change tree so no in-flight foreign work was swept in.
issue.title: Route all main.rs command handlers through a shared pragma-configured connection opener
